 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The Petition-averments are as under:
That on 04.04.2019 at about 7.00 P.M., on B.M.Road, near Silk Farm, Mallipalya,
Kunigal Town, while the Petitioner was proceeding on his Motor-cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-GF-3186 along with one Dinesh as pillion, towards Yediyur, the driver of the Tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-03-C-4543 coming from the opposite-direction drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor-cycle.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous-injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to PHC Kunigal, where he was given first-aid, and was then shifted to A.C.Giri Hospital, B.G.S Nagar, Bellur Cross, Nagamangala Taluk.
The petitioner has spent Rs.1,65,000/- towards medical-treatment, conveyance and incidental expenses.
3. Prior to accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Mechanic in a Garage.
Due to the accident, he sustained grievous-injuries and permanent disablement.
4. That Respondent no.1 being the owner and Respondent no.2 being the Insurer of the offending Tempo are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence this Petition.
5. Despite service of notice, Respondent no.1 remained absent and has been placed exparte.
Respondent No.2-Insurer appeared through its counsel and filed the objections to main petition.
6. In its Objection Statement, Respondent No.2-Insurer has denied that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tempo.
Respondent no.2 has also denied the existence of the Insurance in respect of the Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-C-4543.

It is stated that the owner of the Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-C-4543 had issued the cheque bearing no.208325 dated 30.03.2019 towards the premium amount of Rs.24,776/- ; that the said cheque was dishonoured with an endorsement 'Funds Insufficient', and thus it cancelled the Policy from the date of its inception, by issuing notice to the Owner/Respondent no.1 as well as the RTO; that the Owner/Respondent no.1 is aware of the cancellation of Policy.

That respondent no.2 is thus not liable to indemnify Respondent no.1.
7.
It is further contended that owner of the insured tempo has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
That the driver of tempo had no valid driving licence to drive the tempo and the owner of the vehicle has entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid and effective driving licence.

That accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and he was not wearing any protective Srinivas vs Nagaraj on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33524667/
2 head/gear/helmet while riding the motor cycle.
On these grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 04.04.2019 at about 7.00 p.m. at NH-75 road in front of Reshme Office, Kunigal Town, Tumkur District, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-C- 4543?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
9. In support of his case, the Petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to P.13.
On the other hand, Respondent no.2 has examined a witness as RW.1 and Exs.R.1 to 7 have been marked.
10. Perused the pleadings, oral & documentary evidence on record.
Heard both-sides.

My answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Negative  Issue No. 2 :

In the Negative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 11. Issue No. 1 & 2 : It is the case of Petitioner that he has sustained grievous-injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 04.04.2019 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-C-4543.
On the other hand, Respondent no.2-Insurer has denied that the accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
It has also denied the existence of Policy stating that the Policy has been cancelled owing to dishonour of cheque given by the owner of the tempo/respondent no.1 towards the payment of premium.
That respondent no.2 is thus not liable to compensate the petitioner.
12. In support of his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and Exs.P.1 to 13 have been marked.
On the other hand, respondent no.2 has got its Legal Manager examined as RW.1 and Exs.R.1 to 7 have been marked.

sentences.text: PW.1 has reiterated the petition-averments in the affidavit filed in lieu of his examination-in-chief.
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR & Complaint which show that Ramakrishnaiah - the father of Petitioner has lodged the Complaint on 11.04.2019 i.e., 7 days after the alleged accident.

14. Exs.P.2 & 3 are the Spot Mahazar & Seizure Mahazar drawn by the concerned Police, which describes the alleged accident spot, and seizure of the vehicles viz., Canter Tempo bearing Reg.
No.KA-03-C-4543 and the Motor-cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-JF-3188, alleged to be involved in the accident.
Here it is relevant to note that the said vehicles have been seized in the premises of the Police Station and not at the spot.
As per the IMV Report at Ex.P.5, the petitioner's vehicle as well as the alleged offending Tempo have been damaged.

Ex.P.6 is the true copy of Charge sheet filed against one Raghu - the Driver of the Canter Tempo bearing Reg. No.KA-03-C-4543 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
15.

Next, as per the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.4, the petitioner has sustained:
1. Lacerated wound measuring 6x0.5 x 0.5 cm. Seen over right groin.
2. Lacerated wound measuring 3 x 0.5 x 1 cm.
Seen over left heel.
3. Large abrasion present over exterior aspect of right fore arm and left gluteal area.

4. Hematoma measuring 4 x 3 cm. Seen over right parital eminence.
5.
Free mobility present over right fore arm lower end.
6. Right fore arm both bone distal end fracture.
7. Right trapegium fracture.
8. Right blunt haematic fracture.
It is relevant to note that the Wound certificate at Ex.P.4 is not first in point of time.

It has been obtained by the I.O later; in the absence of MLC & Police Intimation, the wound certificate at Ex.P.4 which provides that the injuries at Sl.Nos.6 to 8 have been shown on the basis of the Discharge Summary of Adichunchanagiri Hospital, does not prove the alleged accident.
16. I shall now discuss the crucial oral & documentary evidence on record.

That as per the FIR and Complaint at Exs.P.1 & 2, the complaint has been lodged by Ramakrishnaiah Srinivas vs Nagaraj on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33524667/
4 - Father of Petitioner at Kunigal Police Station on 11.04.2019, and the case has been registered against the Driver of the Tempo for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the Complaint at Ex.P.1 are as under:
"    -03--4543      .          
     
         
         
 .     
            
       
."
17.

Thus the averments of the Complaint at Ex.P.2 show that:
i) the accident is alleged to have occurred on 04.04.2019 whereas the complaint has been lodged on 11.04.2019 i.e., with delay of 7 days.
ii) that the pillion-rider - Dinesh is stated to have called the Complainant/Father of petitioner over phone and informed of the accident;
iii) the Complainant/Father of petitioner is stated to have visited the accident spot and seen the vehicles, while the petitioner was undergoing treatment at Kunigal Government Hospital; if so, why was the complaint not lodged on the same day???
Why is there no MLC or Police Intimation???

iv) that the petitioner is stated to have been taken to A.C.Giri Hospital B.G.S.Nagara,
Bellur Cross, for further treatment, but when?? not stated.
Thus there is absolutely no document to show that, soon after the accident, the petitioner had been treated at the Government Hospital, Kunigal.
18. Next according to Petitioner/PW.1, immediately after the accident, the petitioner had been taken to Government Hospital, Kunigal.

If at all there had been an accident and the petitioner had indeed been taken to Government Hospital, Kunigal, immediately thereafter, MLC would have been registered and Intimation to Police would have been sent by the said Hospital.
But neither the MLC nor the Police Intimation issued by the Government Hospital, Kunigal, has been placed on record.

Thus in the absence of vital documents, the Spot & Seizure Mahazars at Ex.P.3, Discharge summaries at Exs.P.9 & 11, Wound Certificate at Ex.P.4 and IMV Report at Ex.P.5, all of which have come into existence after the filing of complaint belatedly, cannot be believed.
In turn, the Charge sheet at Ex.P.6 filed wholly based on the basis of the complaint at Ex.P.1, is doubtful.

sentences.text: In view of the above, neither the police documents nor the evidence on record can be believed.
MLC and Police Intimation were the vital documents to prove the accident, moreso when all the Police documents have come into existence after the filing of complaint belatedly.
20. Thus there is no document to show that there was an accident, and immediately thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital.
This renders the accident as well as the involvement of vehicles doubtful.
Thus Respondent no.1- Owner of the alleged offending Tempo has cleverly remained exparte.

21. Next, as per the claim petition, having sustained the injuries (as stated in the wound certificate at Ex.P.4 referred above) the petitioner has been treated as an inpatient from 04.04.2019 to 03.05.2019 and has been subjected to surgery for internal fixation & external fixation to the fractured area at Adichunchanagiri Hospital.

In this regard, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 - Prescriptions - 61, Ex.P.8 - Medical Bills - 68, Discharge summaries at Exs.P.9 & 11, Inpatient Bill at Ex.P.10, OPD Slip at Ex.P.12, and 14 Medical Bills at Ex.P.13.

But it is relevant to note that, as per the Discharge summary at Ex.P.9, the petitioner has been treated conservatively; whereas the Discharge summary at Ex.P.11 pertains to the alleged removal of implants of Right Forearm.
Further, the petitioner has neither examined the doctor nor has produced any X-Ray or the documents to show that he had indeed sustained fractures and has undergone surgery for the same

,
as contended.
The above aspects render the contention of petitioner false that he has sustained grievous injury.

22. On the other hand, the only contention of respondent no.2-Insurance Company is that it is not liable to indemnify the owner of the offending Tempo since the Policy was not in existence as on the date of accident owing to its cancellation due to dishonour of cheque given by the owner of the tempo/respondent no.1 towards the payment of premium.
In support of this contention, respondent no.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW.1 and has got marked Exs.R.1 to 7.
Ex.R.1 is the Authorisation letter, Ex.R.2 is the Cheque dated 30.03.2019, Ex.R.3 is the Cheque Return Memo which shows the date of Presentment as 15.04.2019 and date of Return as 16.04.2019.
Ex.R.4 is the List showing the Dishonoured/Bounced Cheques given towards payment of Premium by Nagaraju - the owner of Tempo/

Respondent no.1, Ex.R.5 is the Letter/Intimation dated 19.04.2019 sent by Respondent no.2-Insurer to Insured/Respondent no.1 regarding the dishonour of cheque given by him towards the payment of premium, and also seeking to return the Insurance Policy immediately.

Ex.R.6 is the Letter/Intimation dated 19.04.2019 sent by Respondent no.2-Insurer to Insured/Respondent no.1 regarding the Cancellation of the Policy issued in respect of the offending Tempo bearing no.KA- 03-C-4543.
Ex.R.7 is the copy of Insurance Policy.

Thus, the cheque dated 30.03.2019 has been presented for encashment on 15.03.2019 and it has been dishonoured with an endorsement 'Insufficient funds' on 16.03.2019, whereas the alleged accident has occurred on 04.04.2019.
But, when the alleged accident and involvement of vehicles itself is doubtful, the question of considering the above defence does not arise.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 & 2 in the "Negative".
24. Issue No.3 :

In view of my findings on Issue no.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of M.V. Act is dismissed.
Draw Award accordingly.
